---
title: "The live preview loop"
---

The reason qmd-fast exists is the edit loop: change the source, and the preview
reflects it *immediately* — without reloading the page, losing your scroll, or
resetting any live content already on screen.

## Incremental updates

On every save the server re-parses the document, diffs the new block list against
the old one by content-hash id, and pushes **only the blocks that changed** over a
websocket. An unchanged block is never touched, so:

- your scroll position is preserved,
- a running Observable cell or Three.js canvas keeps its state,
- the page never flashes white.

The block you just edited **pulses** briefly when it re-renders, so your eye (or
your phone) lands on the change.

## Click-to-source and editor sync

In the browser preview, a plain click browses normally; **Alt-click (Option-click
on Mac) any block to open its exact source line in your editor** (including across
`{{< include >}}`d files) via a `vscode://` deep link (VS Code is assumed for now). The client also speaks a `qmd-goto` / `qmd-cursor`
`postMessage` protocol, so an embedded editor (a VS Code extension, say) can host
the preview and add reverse cursor sync — highlighting the block under your
cursor — without forking anything.

## Live-edit feedback

The loop surfaces what is happening without you watching the terminal:

- The control bar shows a live **word count and reading time** for the prose.
- A non-fatal problem (a broken `{{< include >}}`, a missing kernel, a typo'd
  extension, a **broken `[@citation]` or `@cross-reference`**) appears as a small
  **diagnostics** note in the corner.
- A **broken front matter** points right at the bad line: the diagnostic shows a
  small code frame and is clickable to open that line in your editor.
- A *failed* render throws a prominent, dismissible **error overlay** over the
  last good content, so a broken save is impossible to miss. It clears on the
  next successful render.
- The watcher follows the whole document, not just the served file: editing an
  included subsection, the `.bib`, or **theme CSS** refreshes the preview too —
  and a theme/CSS edit **hot-swaps in place** (no reload), so your scroll position
  and the current slide survive.

## Reading on any screen

The reading layout is responsive, so the same document works on a laptop and a
phone. Wide tables, long code, display math, and embedded canvases scroll within
their own box instead of stretching the page; type and spacing tighten on narrow
screens; in-page links scroll smoothly; and everything honours
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

On a phone the table of contents becomes a **pull-up sheet**: a quiet handle at
the bottom edge that you drag up (or tap) to open the contents, with the current
section flashing in as you scroll. It is keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly
(Enter/Space to open, Escape to close).

To see it on a real device, start the server with `--host`:

```sh
cargo run -p qmd-fast-server -- preview docs/ --host
```

That binds your LAN, prints a `network` URL, and renders a **QR code** in the
terminal. Scan it and the *live* preview opens on your phone, updating as you edit
on your laptop.

Pressing <kbd>Cmd/Ctrl-P</kbd> gives a clean print/PDF: the control bar, TOC
handle, and diagnostics are hidden, the palette forces light, and content flows
full width without clipping code, tables, or math.
